newsitem.title: UK: UK wheat exports up in 1995/96, barley declines.
newsitem.headline: UK wheat exports up in 1995/96, barley declines.

text.p: UK wheat exports in the 1995/96 season rose 20 percent to 3.054 million tonnes while barley exports declined 12 percent to 1.320 million, according to Customs figures and the European Union (EU) trade body Intrastat.
The summary of figures were published by the Home Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) in a weekly digest.
It said over 2.5 million tonnes of wheat exports were accounted for by intra-EU trade with the majority -- 906,069 tonnes -- going to Spain.

Barley exports to EU countries increased sharply last season whilst shipments to third countries suffered a blow from restrictive European Union export policies. Non-EU trade stood at just 4,143 tonnes.
Total wheat imports for 1995/96 were put at 948,000 tonnes, up eight percent from the previous season. Almost two thirds came from other EU countries, mainly Germany and France.
France was also the primary source of maize imports into the UK, supplying 1.018 million tonnes of the total 1.096 million tonnes.
